questions.q: What is the key architectural difference between MySQL and SQL Server/Oracle/PostgreSQL described in this lesson?
options: MySQL splits into a server layer and a pluggable storage engine layer, while the other three each have exactly one storage engine baked in
MySQL has no optimizer at all
SQL Server also supports pluggable storage engines chosen per table
MySQL and the other three all work identically at the storage layer
questions.explain: MySQL's storage engine is a swappable component behind a generic engine API; the other three platforms have a single, fixed storage engine.

questions.q: Which of these is the server layer's responsibility, per this lesson?
options: Connection handling, SQL parsing, and query optimization
Deciding whether rows are locked at the row or table level
Physically writing rows to disk
Implementing foreign key constraints
questions.explain: The server layer handles everything before storage — connections, parsing, and the optimizer — independent of which storage engine is underneath.

questions.q: How is a table's storage engine selected in MySQL?
options: With an ENGINE = clause on CREATE TABLE (or ALTER TABLE to change it later)
It's a server-wide setting that applies to every table
It's fixed permanently at MySQL installation and can never change
It's chosen automatically based on table size
questions.explain: Engine choice is a per-table CREATE TABLE / ALTER TABLE clause, which is exactly why different tables in the same database can use different engines.

options: Lists every storage engine compiled into the running MySQL server and indicates the default
Changes the storage engine of every table in the database
Displays the current query execution plan
Lists all active client connections
questions.explain: SHOW ENGINES; is an informational command showing which engines are available and which one is the default.

questions.q: Why does the statement 'these two tables use different storage engines' make sense for a MySQL database but not for a SQL Server database, per this lesson?
options: SQL Server has exactly one storage engine for the whole product, so there's no per-table engine choice to make
SQL Server tables don't store data on disk
MySQL doesn't actually allow mixing storage engines in practice
SQL Server also has pluggable engines but calls them something else
questions.explain: SQL Server's storage engine is a fixed part of the product; there is no ENGINE = clause or equivalent per-table choice.
